verdict.summary: Agent correctly counted Digital Realty sites in Sydney and Melbourne but wrongly included Port Hedland by treating a new-facility opening as added capacity.
The agent delivered a correct but insufficiently fast numba RK45 solver (~484× aggregate speedup), well below the required 1200× pass threshold.
The agent partially inferred the ball-in-tube rolling rule but mis-placed two of five balls and left a stale tube cell, so the verifier's FAIL is correct.
The agent produced a mostly correct wire-routing grid but mis-layered three wall-crossing cells in row 7, so the verifier's FAIL is correct.
Agent submitted 5.25e-08 after choosing the wrong density aggregation despite computing a passing alternative of 1.13e-07.
The agent submitted 20% from global-mean-normalized t-tests, but the correct answer is 28% from raw Ct testing on the profiling cohort.
Agent submitted 0% after GSEA/ORA pipelines found no FDR-significant immune pathways, but the correct answer is 25% (1 of 4 non-control conditions).
The agent fit a plausible ordered-logit model but submitted OR 1.05, far outside the correct 0.74–0.77 range, due to event-level COVID rows and predictor coding choices.
The agent built a real finite-volume NS solver but official evaluation nRMSE 0.074 missed the 0.0125 bar, so the verifier FAIL is correct.
The agent correctly computed 2023 BFS canton migration-background averages (28.4% landlocked, 42.4% border), but the verifier's ground truth (27.7/42.0) does not match those 2023 figures.
The agent restored the full col() feature and passed 27 self-run tests, but the verifier guardrail reported no git-detectable code changes and never ran pytest.
The agent fully executed the Film Production Day adaptability workflow, but the verifier failed it for one extra confirmation email that strict tool-count matching treats as an automatic zero.
Agent completed saves and outbound email but never handled the required adaptability reply, exhausting the simulation before Kritsana's change request could arrive.
The agent completed the full adaptability workflow, but the verifier scored only 4/7 oracle action matches and failed the rollout.
The agent completed the unambiguous chores but then purchased the ambiguous board game instead of stopping at a clarifying question, so the verifier's FAIL is correct.
The agent handled only one of two in-window Kjersti emails, ordered one sand-art kit instead of two, and never created the conditional calendar event.
The agent emailed the detective but never notified with the required phrase, missed the follow-up lawyer workflow, and never forwarded harassment emails, so the verifier's FAIL is correct.

The agent implemented a real contiguous-select optimization with large measured speedup and verified equivalence, but the verifier recorded an empty patch due to a broken git artifact and never ran performance grading.
The agent delivered a functionally correct isalpha C-ufunc speedup over baseline, but its patch was slightly slower than the reference commit and well below the 1.7× pass threshold.
The agent delivered correct but partial merge optimizations (~3x) that fell far short of the reference monotonic-key fast path (~47x), so the verifier's FAIL is justified.
The agent shipped a correct but incomplete Period.strftime fast path that passed equivalence checks yet fell well short of the reference commit's speed on the held-out benchmark suite.
The agent shipped a correct but suboptimal pure-Python early-exit optimization that fell well short of the reference Cython fix and the 1.2× speedup threshold.
The agent's enum fast-path broke validation of enum-member inputs, so the verifier's functional-equivalence failure is correct.
The agent produced an incorrect closed-form answer due to an algebraic error in its feasibility inequality, and the verifier's LLM-judge FAIL is correct.
The agent produced n₀/|t|² ≈ 8.20, but the correct value is (4/9)(17−8cos(2√3)) ≈ 10.93, so the verifier's FAIL is justified.
The agent nailed X₁ and X₂ but omitted the universally-closed tag on X₃, so the LLM verifier correctly scored reward 0.
The agent misidentified the beach photo as Seattle instead of Tacoma, and the LLM-as-judge verifier correctly awarded reward 0.
The agent misidentified a Sophoridine structure diagram as Matrine, so the verifier's FAIL is correct.
The agent nailed babylonian vocalization, parchment, and 1chr.004:009 from image analysis but submitted 08-14 instead of the correct 10-16 century span, so the verifier's FAIL is justified.
The agent submitted 4 steps (letter D) but panel D shows only two steps where R414Q clearly exceeds the triple mutant, so the verifier's INCORRECT is right.
Agent correctly implemented PWM loading and KLD but its generate_dna diverges from the required construction, causing Step 76.4 scan_sequence integration tests to fail.
The agent implemented plausible but incorrect Gaussian-beam physics, failed all three hidden sub-step checks, and the verifier's FAIL is correct.
The agent implemented init_eji_array correctly but integrate_DOS lacks the required tetrahedron-volume normalization and uses an incorrect middle-band formula, so the verifier's FAIL is justified.
The agent produced a serious scaling-law fit but its hidden-test R² of 0.983 fell short of the 0.995 extrapolation gate, so the verifier's FAIL is correct.
The agent built runnable dbt models but its deduplication change and Haversine fix produced output tables that do not match the gold standard, so the verifier's FAIL is correct.
The agent added middleware helpers and self-tests, but left the interceptor unwired, chose the wrong default version, and its test-file edits prevented the verifier from grading.

The agent implemented the correct Play hosts validation fix, but the verifier spuriously failed because staging the gold test patch aborted after the agent had already applied the same runme.sh change.

The agent added the suffix workaround but its version_check(compiled=False) calls are incompatible with the official tests, and the verifier never ran pytest because the agent's test edits blocked gold test_patch staging.
The agent made no code changes, wrongly concluded the refactor was already merged, and left the base tree missing dialEndpoint/kubeClusterEndpoint/kubeAddress that the held-out tests require.
The agent implemented most signal-termination messaging correctly but left verbose successful-exit notifications without the required :process PID suffix, causing the sole verifier failure.
The agent partially fixed annotate xy copying but left OffsetFrom._ref_coord mutable, so the verifier correctly failed the held-out image-comparison test.
The agent partially fixed parent-link selection in base.py but left options.py unchanged, so held-out MTI tests still crash with ImproperlyConfigured.
Verifier never ran tests (sandbox timeout); the agent shipped an unrelated F-expression ordering tweak and did not implement the add_select_col fix the task requires.
The agent's dataLim-restore patch left interactive SpanSelector still forcing axis bounds to include 0, so the verifier's FAIL is correct.
The agent emitted desc_sig_keyword nodes for Literal booleans instead of plain text, so the held-out Literal annotation test failed.
The agent added a minimal int32 stack dtype regression test, but SWTBench correctly failed the rollout because the harness reported resolved=false with zero differential coverage of the gold fix.
The agent produced a single biologically plausible primer pair but its forward/reverse Tm spread is ~7°C under oligotm on verifier-defined annealing regions, violating the ≤5°C constraint.
